title: Deep learning ECG model separates Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI, with a randomized reader study
summary: A self-supervised three-architecture ensemble reached AUC 0.970 and 0.914 accuracy on external validation (95 participants from two institutions). In a randomized four-phase reader study with 70 readers, AI assistance raised the probability of correct diagnosis from 0.632 to 0.864 (OR 3.71); the source notes AI-assisted accuracy stayed below model accuracy.
ai_technology: Self-supervised deep learning ensemble with Grad-CAM explanations

evidence.tested: External validation on 95 participants from two institutions, and a four-phase reader study in which 70 readers were randomized to reference sheet, AI predictions, or AI with Grad-CAM.
evidence.unknown: Exploratory reader-background analyses; preprint not yet peer reviewed; reader AI-assisted accuracy below model accuracy.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble classified 12-lead ECG images; its predictions and Grad-CAM maps were shown to readers.
